name: membrane-actin-ratchet
title: Membrane–actin Brownian ratchet — from boundary baselines to a coupled flexible membrane
lead:
This investigation builds and validates a multiscale Brownian ratchet in which growing actin
filaments push a membrane forward. We climb a staircase of boundary realism and, at the top
rung, put the actin↔membrane coupler itself under the microscope. The payoff is the headline
benchmark: a closed-loop force/velocity curve that only a flexible membrane can produce.

at_a_glance.role: Rung 1 — reproduces the classical rigid-wall ratchet (velocity≈0, force accumulates) as the controlled baseline.
Rung 2 — a movable rigid object with drag introduces load-dependent stalling bounded by Peskin 1993.
Coupler direction A — verifies interface forces are equal-and-opposite (Newton's 3rd law).
Coupler direction B — verifies membrane→actin position feedback preserves mesh quality and box potentials.
Rung 3 — the deformable membrane inflates under actin load, relaxing contact force off the rigid curve.
Headline benchmark — the closed loop reproduces the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition.

how_to_read:
Dependency ladder (reading order):
  Fixed Wall → Rigid Wall → Force Handshake → Feedback → Flexible Membrane → F-V Benchmark
The two boundary baselines and the two coupler directions are independent tracks that converge on
the flexible rung; read them in the order above for the narrative, but note the DAG is convergent,
not a single chain.

Each study is organized around ONE decision figure that carries its expected pattern and acceptance
threshold — that figure determines pass/fail. Open the other charts only to interrogate a verdict.

Conclusion labels used throughout:
  OBSERVED  — measured directly in a run.
  INFERRED  — expected from theory/design, NOT yet measured here.
  VALIDATED — measured AND matched to a benchmark within threshold.
Nothing is VALIDATED yet. Today the charts mostly show that simulations execute; treat them as
workflow-readiness evidence, not confirmed results.

glossary.definition: Mechanism converting thermal fluctuations at a barrier into directed motion when polymerization rectifies the transient gap.
Force–velocity relationship of the advancing barrier; its shape (concave vs convex) is the diagnostic signature.
Closed-form theory for a Brownian ratchet against a rigid load; sets the rigid-rung expectations.
Flexible-membrane ratchet study showing a concave→convex F-V transition with polymerization rate — the headline benchmark.
Mesh-based discrete-differential-geometry membrane simulator providing the deformable boundary.
Particle-based reaction-diffusion simulator providing the actin filaments and tip dynamics.
The composite Step that exchanges tip forces and boundary positions between ReaDDy and Mem3DG each tick.

biological_story:
In a crawling or dividing cell, networks of actin filaments polymerize against the plasma
membrane and push it forward. The Brownian-ratchet picture explains how directed motion arises
without a molecular motor: thermal fluctuations transiently open a gap between a filament tip and
the barrier, a monomer adds into that gap, and the new subunit rectifies the fluctuation into net
forward displacement. How much force the network can deliver, and how fast the barrier advances,
depends critically on what the filaments are pushing against.

Against a *rigid wall* the problem is classical: each filament ratchets independently and the
force/velocity relation follows Peskin's 1993 theory. Let the barrier *move* as a rigid object
with drag, and a load-dependent stalling regime appears — the wall advances at a velocity set by
the balance between contact force and drag. But a real membrane is neither fixed nor rigid: it
*deforms*. Curvature lets the membrane redistribute load across many nearby filaments, relaxing
the burden on any single tip and breaking the per-filament independence the rigid theories assume.

Capturing that requires two simulators talking to each other every step: ReaDDy supplies the
particle-based actin filaments and their tip dynamics; Mem3DG supplies the deformable, mesh-based
membrane. The BrownianRatchetCoupler is the interface — it must translate actin tip forces into
membrane vertex loads and feed updated membrane positions back as actin boundary constraints,
without violating Newton's third law, without degrading mesh quality, and without breaking
ReaDDy's reaction balance. Only when that handshake is faithful does the coupled system reach the
diagnostic flexible-membrane signature: the concave→convex force/velocity transition that Inoue
et al. (2015) report and that no rigid barrier can reproduce.
question:
Can a particle-based actin Brownian ratchet (ReaDDy) push against a deformable membrane
(Mem3DG) through a physically faithful bidirectional coupler, and does increasing boundary
realism — fixed wall → rigid movable object → flexible membrane — reproduce the
force/velocity signatures that distinguish a flexible-membrane ratchet (Inoue 2015) from
the classical rigid-wall regime (Peskin 1993)?
hypothesis:
Boundary realism changes the F-V relationship in a structured, predictable way.
(1) The fixed wall reproduces classical Brownian-ratchet kinetics (velocity ≈ 0, contact
force accumulates). (2) The rigid movable object introduces a load-dependent stalling regime
bounded by Peskin (1993). (3) The flexible Mem3DG membrane qualitatively diverges in the
high-load regime because curvature redistributes force across nearby filaments, breaking the
per-filament independence the rigid models assume — but only if the actin↔membrane coupler is
faithful: equal-and-opposite interface forces (Newton's 3rd law), bounded per-step
displacements that preserve mesh quality, and a closed loop that reaches the Inoue-2015
concave→convex transition.

executive.what_is_this:
An investigation is a sequence of studies that together answer one research question. This
one asks whether a coupled actin (ReaDDy) + membrane (Mem3DG) composite behaves like a real
flexible-membrane Brownian ratchet, by comparing three boundary models and stress-testing the
coupler that powers the flexible one. It merges two earlier framings — a boundary-condition
staircase and a coupling-mechanism deep-dive — into one arc, because the staircase's top rung
*is* the coupler the deep-dive validates.
executive.verdict:
WORKFLOW-READY, NOT YET VALIDATED. All six studies execute end-to-end and emit observables —
the strongest supported conclusion today is that the coupled ReaDDy↔Mem3DG pipeline runs, not
that any biological or physical hypothesis has been confirmed. No acceptance test has been
evaluated; no benchmark comparison (Peskin 1993, Inoue 2015) has been run. The arc is wired;
the verdicts are pending.
executive.verdict_detail:
Decision figures now exist for four studies (fixed-boundary, rigid-movable-boundary,
coupled-ratchet-cycle-fv-reproduction, actin-to-membrane-force-handshake), each carrying its
expected pattern, on-plot acceptance threshold, and a NOT-YET-VALIDATED stamp (see each study's
decision_figure + guidelines.visual_design). First real signal: fixed-boundary shows mean
barrier_velocity = 0 → PASS on the velocity≈0 criterion. gate_status is null (no dependency
block). The remaining blockers are now DATA-EMISSION gaps, not plotting: (1) run params don't
record growth_rate / barrier_drag, so the F-V and stall sweeps can't be separated; (2) the
membrane side emits no integrated reaction force/impulse, so the Newton-3rd-law residual is not
computable; (3) mesh-quality / curvature need face connectivity + per-vertex fields emitted.
Next: close these emitter gaps and re-run, then the stub tests can become evaluated predicates;
and source the Peskin/Inoue reference curves so the overlays stop being schematic.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
Boundary realism is the controlling variable for the actin-ratchet F-V relationship, and a
faithful Mem3DG↔ReaDDy coupler is necessary to recover the flexible-membrane regime that rigid
models cannot produce.
evidence_for: [OBSERVED] Fixed and rigid rungs share one actin model; only the barrier changes — a clean controlled comparison, and both run.
[OBSERVED] In the fixed rung barrier_velocity holds at ~0 while contact_force accumulates.
[OBSERVED] In the flexible rung the vesicle inflates under actin pressure.
[INFERRED] Closed-form Peskin (1993) expectations bracket the two rigid rungs — falsifiable, but the comparison has not been run.
evidence_against: [OPEN] All acceptance tests are still stubs; no quantitative match has been demonstrated.
[OPEN] The concave→convex F-V transition (Inoue 2015) is asserted by construction, not measured — vesicle inflation alone is NOT evidence of ratchet behavior.
[OPEN] Newton's-3rd-law balance and mesh-quality preservation are inferred from design, not yet measured.

fixed-boundary — tip–wall gap distribution + contact-force accumulation vs Peskin (to-build)
membrane-to-actin-displacement-feedback — mesh-quality metrics, gentle vs aggressive (to-build)
caveats: The strongest supported conclusion today is WORKFLOW READINESS, not biological validation.
Coupler faithfulness (Newton's 3rd law, mesh quality) is a precondition; if it fails the F-V comparison is uninterpretable.
ReaDDy reaction balance under per-step boundary updates is assumed, not yet proven.
Current visuals emphasize that simulations ran; they do not yet reveal the mechanism (gap formation, force transfer, load redistribution).

studies.name: fixed-boundary
studies.title: Rung 1 · Fixed boundary
studies.question: Does the composite reproduce the rigid-wall Peskin-1993 regime — Brownian-ratchet kinetics against an immovable boundary — to within numerical tolerance, when barrier_kind is "fixed"?

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does an immovable barrier produce pure force accumulation with no advance (the classical rigid-wall ratchet limit)?
resolved_uncertainties: Against a fixed wall the barrier velocity holds at ~0 while contact force accumulates (OBSERVED).
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the gap-distribution / ratchet event rate quantitatively match Peskin (1993) — not yet compared to theory.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: The accumulating contact_force is an artefact of wall stiffness (force_constant), not genuine Brownian-ratchet rectification.
evidence_for: contact_force scales with force_constant by construction.
evidence_against: barrier_velocity ~0 and a thermal-fluctuation-shaped gap distribution would argue for true ratcheting.

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Confirms the rigid-wall baseline: a fixed barrier converts polymerization into accumulated force, not motion.

followup_study_proposals.title: Quantify the tip-wall gap distribution against Peskin theory
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: Turns the OBSERVED velocity~0 into a VALIDATED match (or refutation) of the rigid-wall ratchet rate.

studies.claim: OBSERVED (partial pass): against an immovable wall mean barrier_velocity = 0 (within ±1e-3) while contact force accumulates. Quantitative match to the Peskin ratchet rate still pending a digitized reference.

studies.name: rigid-movable-boundary
studies.title: Rung 2 · Rigid movable boundary
studies.question: With barrier_kind="rigid_movable", does the wall translate at a velocity proportional to the mean contact force (drag-balance Peskin 1993 setup), and does the stall force remain bounded?

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does a drag-loaded movable barrier exhibit load-dependent stalling within the Peskin (1993) bound?
resolved_uncertainties: A movable wall settles to a non-zero steady velocity (8/8 runs, OBSERVED).
remaining_uncertainties: Stall force vs the Peskin closed-form ceiling is unchecked; barrier_drag is recorded for only 2/8 runs so the drag sweep is not separable.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: Steady velocity reflects the imposed drag balance (dz/dt=F/drag) rather than ratchet-limited advance.
evidence_for: velocity tracks 1/drag by construction in the two tagged runs.
evidence_against: a Peskin-consistent stall force at high drag would indicate genuine load-dependent ratcheting.

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Adds a drag-balance stalling regime between the fixed wall and the flexible membrane.

followup_study_proposals.title: Drag sweep with barrier_drag recorded in run params + Peskin stall-bound overlay
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: Separates the low/high-drag conditions and tests the stall force against theory.

studies.claim: OBSERVED: a drag-loaded movable wall settles to a non-zero velocity. Whether the stall force stays within the Peskin-1993 bound is NOT yet checked.

studies.name: actin-to-membrane-force-handshake
studies.title: Coupler A · Actin→membrane force handshake
studies.question: In the closed-loop flexible composite, is the force the actin side reports at the interface equal-and-opposite to the force the membrane integrates on its receiving vertices (Newton's 3rd law on the coupling interface)?

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Is the actin→membrane coupling momentum-faithful (Newton's 3rd law) at the interface?
resolved_uncertainties: Under option B the coupler delivers a membrane pressure-force equal to the actin contact force; force_residual ~0 every step.
remaining_uncertainties: This is magnitude-conservation through the osmotic channel, NOT an independent per-vertex force exchange — option A (a genuine applied force in pymem3dg) is blocked by a binding segfault.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: residual~0 is a bookkeeping identity (offset sized as contact_force/area), not evidence the simulator conserves momentum locally.
evidence_against: an independent readback of the integrated applied force matching contact_force (option A) would be a true check.
discriminating_observables: net force on the closed vesicle

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Coupling transmits the contact-force MAGNITUDE as a global osmotic pressure; locality/momentum is unverified.

followup_study_proposals.title: Option A — apply a genuine local contact force in pymem3dg and read it back

studies.claim: OBSERVED (option B, magnitude-conserving): the coupler now sizes the osmotic offset so its integrated membrane force equals the actin contact force; force_residual ≈ 0 every step. CAVEAT: pressure-mediated effective-force handshake, not an independent per-vertex check (that is option A, blocked by a pymem3dg applied-force segfault — tracked).

studies.name: membrane-to-actin-displacement-feedback
studies.title: Coupler B · Membrane→actin displacement feedback
studies.question: Does per-step mesh-position feedback from Mem3DG to ReaDDy preserve mesh quality (no vertex inversion or degenerate triangles) and keep tip particles within their box-potential bounds?

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does per-step membrane→actin position feedback preserve mesh quality and keep tips inside their box potentials?
remaining_uncertainties: Mesh quality is currently inferred, not measured — runs.db emits vertex positions but not face connectivity / min triangle area / inverted-face count.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: Aggressive feedback gain pushes the boundary past actin tips in one step, degrading the mesh (inverted faces) or violating box potentials.
evidence_for: large osmotic_force_scale moves the boundary far per tick.

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Feedback faithfulness is unverified pending mesh-quality observables.

followup_study_proposals.title: Emit mesh-quality observables and sweep gentle vs aggressive feedback
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: Turns inferred mesh stability into a measured pass/fail.

studies.claim: TARGET (not yet tested): per-step mesh-position feedback preserves mesh quality and keeps tips inside their box potentials. Mesh-quality is currently inferred, not measured.

studies.name: flexible-mem3dg-boundary
studies.title: Rung 3 · Flexible Mem3DG boundary
studies.question: With barrier_kind="flexible" (closed-icosphere Mem3DG mesh inside-pushed by bonded actin filaments), does the membrane deform under actin pressure and relax the contact-force burden compared to the rigid_movable rung?

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does a deformable membrane redistribute actin load and relax contact force off the rigid curve?
resolved_uncertainties: Under actin pressure the vesicle inflates (OBSERVED).
remaining_uncertainties: Load redistribution across filaments and relaxation of per-tip contact force vs the rigid rung are not yet quantified — inflation alone is not ratchet success.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: Vesicle inflation is driven by the osmotic setpoint itself, not by actin pushing — the membrane would inflate without the actin field.
evidence_against: per-tip contact force dropping below the rigid baseline, and curvature concentrating at the contact zone, would indicate genuine load redistribution.
discriminating_observables: mean per-tip contact_force vs rigid rung
curvature map at the contact zone

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Supports a deformable barrier that stores/redistributes load, distinct from the rigid rungs.

followup_study_proposals.title: Rigid-vs-flexible per-tip contact-force comparison + curvature maps (identical camera/scale)
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: Tests whether the membrane actually relaxes load off the rigid curve.

studies.claim: OBSERVED: under actin pressure the vesicle inflates. That load is redistributed across filaments / relaxed off the rigid curve is NOT yet quantified — inflation alone is not ratchet success.

studies.name: coupled-ratchet-cycle-fv-reproduction
studies.title: Benchmark · Coupled force–velocity reproduction
studies.question: Does the closed-loop coupled cycle reproduce the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition as polymerization rate varies — the headline numerical benchmark for a flexible-membrane ratchet (spec §1.2)?

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does the closed loop reproduce the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition that distinguishes a flexible-membrane ratchet?
remaining_uncertainties: The concave→convex transition has not been measured; growth_rate is not recorded in run params so the sweep cannot be separated; no Inoue-2015 overlay yet.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: Any F-V shape change is an artefact of the coupler gain / osmotic mapping rather than genuine flexible-membrane ratchet physics.
evidence_against: a curvature sign-flip that tracks Inoue 2015 across a real growth_rate sweep would argue for the physics.

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: The diagnostic transition is asserted by construction; measuring it is the headline open test.

followup_study_proposals.title: Record growth_rate in run params, run the sweep, and overlay the Inoue-2015 reference
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: The headline VALIDATED/REFUTED verdict for the flexible-membrane ratchet.

studies.claim: TARGET (not yet tested): the closed loop reproduces the Inoue-2015 concave→convex F-V transition. No benchmark comparison has been run.
